name: dropzone
description: Drag-and-drop file input built on the native HTML5 drag-drop API plus a visually-hidden <input type='file'> for keyboard + screen-reader access. Filters by accept/maxSize/maxFiles before emitting.

props.name: onFilesSelected
props.description: Callback fired with the accepted File[] on pick or drop.

props.name: onFilesRejected
props.description: Callback fired with the rejected File[] when files fail accept/maxSize/maxFiles, OR when multiple={false} and extras were sliced off. Receives the rejected File[]. Use to surface 'wrong type' / 'too large' toasts.

props.name: accept
props.description: Accept attribute forwarded to the hidden file input. Three forms: MIME type ('application/pdf'), MIME wildcard ('image/*'), or extension with leading dot ('.csv'). Extension matching is suffix-based (mirrors HTML5) — '.csv' will match 'notes.md.csv' as well.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow multiple files. With `multiple={false}`, the first accepted file flows to onFilesSelected and any extras flow to onFilesRejected so consumers can toast them.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: Cap on the number of accepted files. Excess files are dropped silently — surface in your handler if needed.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Maximum size per file in bytes. Files over the cap are filtered before onFilesSelected fires.

props.name: children
props.description: Render override for the body. Pass a node, or a function receiving { isDragOver, isDisabled, openFileDialog } for layout control.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Required accessible name for the drop area.

slots.name: children
slots.description: Body of the drop area (icon + copy). Optional — sensible default included.

examples.title: Image upload
examples.description: Filter to images only with a 5MB cap

examples.title: Custom body via render prop
examples.description: Take full control of the drop area visuals

ai.whenToUse: Use for any file upload UX where drag-drop is helpful (image uploaders, CSV import, attachment pickers). Built on native HTML5 + a hidden <input type='file'> so keyboard and screen-reader users get the same affordance.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for camera/microphone capture (use <input type='file' capture> directly or a media-specific component). Don't use for chunked/resumable uploads — Dropzone only emits File[]; pair with a real upload pipeline (tus, S3 multipart). Don't use for clipboard paste image upload — listen on document for that.
commonMistakes: Forgetting aria-label — without it the drop area is announced as just 'button' to screen readers
Setting accept='image' (missing the slash or wildcard) — must be a MIME type, MIME prefix with /*, or a .extension
Forgetting that extension matching is suffix-based — '.csv' will match 'notes.md.csv'. Acceptable (mirrors HTML5) but document upstream if business logic requires strict suffix-only
Treating maxFiles as enforcement — files past the cap are dropped silently; if business rules require it, validate again on submit
Forgetting to clear the file input value after a successful upload — Dropzone resets the hidden input automatically; if you wrap it, do the same
Calling preventDefault on parent containers' onDragOver — without it the browser opens the file when dropped on the window outside the dropzone
Treating empty drops as no-op silently when the user expected feedback — pair with onFilesRejected to surface filter failures
ai.accessibilityNotes: The drop area is a role='button' div with tabIndex=0 and the required aria-label; Enter and Space open the file dialog. The file input is visually-hidden but live in the DOM so keyboard focus + assistive-tech file pickers work. Drag-state is exposed via data-drag-over for CSS-only state styling. When disabled, the drop area is removed from the tab order and aria-disabled is set.
